questions.q: What does Schnarch say every committed relationship has?
a: One partner who wants sex more often than the other
A period where desire disappears completely
A shared preference for the same sexual routine
One partner who avoids all physical contact
questions.why: Lesson 1 says every couple has a high desire partner and a low desire partner.

questions.q: Why does the low desire partner hold power, according to the summary?
a: They decide whether the sex their partner wants happens
They are usually the one who earns more money
They are better at hiding their true feelings
They set the rules for every other part of the relationship
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the lower-desire partner controls the frequency, though the role can feel like a burden.

questions.q: Why do long-term couples tend to keep sex the same?
a: Familiar routines keep anxiety down
They lose all physical attraction over time
Doctors advise against changing routines
They no longer care about each other's pleasure
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes the comfort and safety cycle, where routine makes partners feel secure.

questions.q: What happens when partners only stay inside their sexual comfort zone?
a: Even small changes start to feel threatening
Desire returns on its own after a few months
They naturally discover new preferences
Communication improves without extra effort
questions.why: Lesson 2 says staying in the comfort zone makes any change anxiety-inducing, though change keeps things alive.

questions.q: What is hugging until relaxed meant to do?
a: Build a physical alliance and release tension
Replace conversation about sexual problems
Measure how compatible two partners are
Start every sexual encounter the same way
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes ten minutes of slow breathing in an embrace as a tangible symbol of partnership.
